claim_boundary: Deribit currently defines monthly options expiry as the last Friday of each calendar month at 08:00 UTC and applies settlement-specific delivery-price and delta-decay mechanics. These mechanics make a recurring expiry-day liquidity and hedging disturbance plausible, but current documentation does not independently prove that identical monthly rules governed every 2019-2024 observation or that aggregate spot Bitcoin returns are negative on those dates. Exactly one preregistered full-day risk-veto audit may test the calendar proxy; no alpha claim is imported from exchange documentation.

prior_matrix.finding: Deribit states that monthly options expire on the last Friday of each calendar month at 08:00 UTC and distinguishes daily, weekly, monthly and quarterly expiries.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: The current policy page is not a sealed historical listing archive for every monthly expiry from 2019 through 2024.

prior_matrix.finding: Deribit describes expiry delivery at 08:00 UTC, a delivery price based on the 07:30-08:00 UTC index TWAP, and linear decay of expiring option and future delta during the final 30 minutes.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: Settlement mechanics establish a plausible flow event but do not establish its sign, magnitude, persistence or effect on broad spot BTC returns.

real_time_design_requirements: Freeze the exact proleptic Gregorian last-Friday calendar, 00:00 UTC exit, 24-hour cash interval and following-Saturday 00:00 UTC reentry before accessing BTC outcomes.
Use only complete UTC-day events from 2019-01-01 through 2024-12-31 derived without market or options data; reject any month with zero or more than one computed last Friday.
Use the existing sealed 52,608-row BTC H1 corpus and require exact hourly continuity at every exit and reentry boundary.
Charge the same fee and adverse slippage on every exit and reentry under the same capital and final valuation as the matched full-capital BTC buy-and-hold comparator.

Require separate Design and Validation predictive event gates before matched-capital economics; expose event count, median return, negative-rate effect, drawdown path, annual breadth and top-event concentration.
Do not add weekly, quarterly, daily or non-Deribit expiries; option strikes, open interest, implied volatility, max-pain, funding, basis, direction filters or magnitude thresholds.
Do not shift the 24-hour interval around 08:00 UTC, scan neighboring weekdays, invert the veto, add fractional sizing or rescue a failure with a different calendar window.
Do not reinterpret the closed crypto-carry branch as evidence for this family; the proposed feature is a deterministic monthly settlement calendar, not a measured carry state.
Do not open post-2024 data; any historical pass remains REPORTED_NOT_ACTIVATED and requires separately sealed independent OOS.
uncertainty: Historical Deribit monthly-expiry schedule continuity for every 2019-2024 month remains MISSING_PROOF; the audit tests a frozen calendar proxy unless separately proven before outcome access.
A last-Friday effect could reflect month-end portfolio flows rather than options expiry, so mechanism attribution is not identified by calendar returns alone.
The event sample is sparse at approximately twelve days per year, increasing uncertainty and concentration risk.
A full-day cash veto can miss positive BTC convexity and pays two transitions per event; apparent drawdown improvement may be economically dominated by foregone upside and fees.
No BTC return, event outcome, post-2024 observation, hypothesis, candidate, OOS or Trading path was accessed while freezing this prior.
